web.title: The Fourth State: Are We Entering an Era of Attacking Plasma Orbs?
web.note: Wright compares the dangerous-orb stories in three recent bestselling books tied to Skinwalker Ranch and asks whether the orbs are plasma, who benefits from a frightening orb narrative, and what British folklore about helpful brownies and harmful boggarts suggests about how we relate to such beings.

web.title: Seeking humanity's "biggest ever discovery": Avi Loeb in dialogue with Bernardo Kastrup
web.source: Bernardo Kastrup: With Reality in Mind (Amir Giles)
web.note: A two-hour recorded conversation in which Loeb, a materialist focused on instrument data, and Kastrup, who holds that consciousness is fundamental, debate nuts-and-bolts explanations versus Vallée, whether AI could be conscious, and whether proof of non-human intelligence would overturn materialism. Judged from the page description and chapter list; the recording appears to be for paying members.
web.interest: Consciousness; AI and non-human intelligence; Vallée

web.title: 'Archive X' and the impossible | Reality Check
web.note: Rice University scholar Jeffrey Kripal argues that anomalous experiences are not increasing; people are simply more willing to report them, and he places UAP and contact reports inside a wider study of consciousness rather than fear-based government stories. Judged from a third-party summary of the video.

web.title: Is Our Government Being Influenced by Nonhuman Intelligence?
web.note: Author Peter Levenda talks about occultism, mythology, and power, and his own "Men in Black" experience, alongside government-secrecy themes. Only the paywalled preview was readable; ranked low because much of it is cover-up material.
web.interest: Secondary: government secrecy; some occult and consciousness material

items.title: "Boggarts, Brownies, Hobs and their Goblin Kin": 200 goblin figures, including goblins from a UFO
items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.note: Rae's book collects goblin lore worldwide and includes UFO-linked goblin reports, like the Kelly-Hopkinsville case. Book promo.

items.title: In Scots Gaelic lore, fairies were fallen angels, non-human nature spirits, or spirits of the dead
items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.note: Stephen G. Rae on the three old explanations for fairies, a direct parallel to today's debates about what non-human intelligence is.

items.title: Jacques Vallee UFO Control System: Mythology as Social Technology
items.note: Walters recaps Vallée's control-system idea: the phenomenon works like a thermostat on human belief, using absurd, high-strange events to reshape myth, and he suggests people can study the feedback loop instead of watching passively. A recap of Vallée's 1970s ideas rather than new reporting; the page also shows an April update date.

items.title: Follow-up: nobody is discussing Levenda's point about the phenomenon manipulating our consciousness
items.author: @TheUfoJoe
items.note: Murgia argues the alleged manipulation of human consciousness is the most important, and most ignored, part of the debate.

items.title: "The phenomenon manipulates consciousness": Peter Levenda on whether we can defend against it
items.author: @TheUfoJoe
items.note: Murgia quotes occult historian Peter Levenda saying the phenomenon can appear as whatever it wants and alter perception, and that people can resist it.
items.interest: Mind control; consciousness; nature of the phenomenon

items.title: Are some officials under non-human mind control, keeping them from disclosing?

items.note: Murgia weighs Robert Martinez's claims that non-humans influence officials' minds. He rates Martinez's credibility as undetermined; highly speculative.
